name: Mispar
overview: Mispar was a male individual who returned to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra 2:2 and Nehemiah 7:7. He is also referred to as Misperethin in Nehemiah 7:7. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Mispar means "number" in Hebrew, as noted in Ezra 2:2. Another form of his name, Mispereth, appears in Nehemiah 7:7, though its meaning is not specified. Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Mispar was a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader lineage of Israel as noted in Ezra 2:2. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mispar's significance lies in his participation in the return of the exiles to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, marking a pivotal moment in Israel's restoration. His mention in both Ezra and Nehemiah underscores his role among those who helped reestablish the community in the promised land. This return represents a fulfillment of God's promises and a renewal of covenant faithfulness.
